payload.alternatives: Add "main" to scope-enum: turned down, it changes a commitlint rule, and the owner required that no commitlint rule be touched. Raise header-max-length: turned down for the same reason, it relaxes a rule. Change the release-please pull-request-title-pattern so release PRs use an allowed scope: turned down, it changes release tooling and the pattern is also used to recognise earlier release PRs, so it risks duplicate release PRs. Run the check on every PR including bots: turned down, release-please PRs would fail on scope-enum (CI does run on them) and a long Dependabot title would fail on header length, with no way to fix either from the PR. Rely only on the local husky commit-msg hook: turned down, squash merges bypass it.
payload.rationale: Merges are squash-only, so the PR title is the commit that lands on main, and the local commit-msg hook never sees it. A CI step (workflow Commitlint, job "PR title") now runs commitlint with commitlint.config.js on the PR title, so Conventional Commits is enforced by the machine where it matters. The step is skipped when the PR author is dependabot[bot] or github-actions[bot] (release-please). Bots write their own titles: release-please titles its PRs "chore(main): release ..." and "main" is not in scope-enum, and Dependabot titles can reach the 100-character header-max-length (the phpstan bump PR was exactly 100). The skip is keyed on the PR author, not on who triggered the event, so a person editing a bot PR's title does not turn the check off. No commitlint rule was changed: these PRs are not checked, nothing is relaxed. Landed in PR #141 (merge commit 949eb6d); the skip was added to that PR before merge. Observed afterwards: the check shows as SKIPPED on Dependabot PRs.
payload.title: Run the commitlint PR-title check only for human-authored PRs

payload.alternatives: Move to mermaid 12 anyway with --legacy-peer-deps or an npm override: turned down, it forces a combination the plugin does not declare support for and hides the conflict instead of resolving it. Replace or drop vitepress-plugin-mermaid so mermaid 12 can be used: turned down, it is a docs-tooling change far larger than the version bump and was not requested. Leave the mermaid 12 PR open: turned down, it can never go green and Dependabot would keep refreshing it.
payload.rationale: vitepress-plugin-mermaid (latest 2.0.17) declares the peer dependency mermaid "10 || 11", so mermaid 12 cannot be installed alongside it; the Dependabot PR for mermaid 12.1.0 (#135) could never install. mermaid stays on 11 (the root package.json range ^11.17.0), and .github/dependabot.yml now ignores version-update:semver-major for mermaid in the npm ecosystem (PR #141). Dependabot closed #135 on its own as soon as the ignore reached main, and a comment recording the reason was left on it. Minor and patch updates inside 11 still arrive normally (11.17.0 to 11.17.2 was merged in the npm group). Revisit once the plugin widens its peer range.
payload.title: Hold mermaid at 11 and ignore semver-major mermaid updates in Dependabot

payload.alternatives: Adopt vitest 5 now and lower the mutation break threshold: turned down, the floor must not be lowered. Adopt vitest 5 with a local patch of @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner (patch-package): turned down, the separator patch only reaches about 78% on one file against 85% on vitest 4, so it is not parity, and it would add a vendor patch to maintain. Adopt vitest 5 and skip mutation testing: turned down, mutation is a CI gate. Keep the Dependabot PRs for vitest and coverage-v8 separate: turned down, a mixed-version install fails and neither can pass alone. Wait without an ignore entry: turned down, Dependabot would keep opening vitest 5 PRs that cannot pass.
payload.rationale: Measured on a clean npm ci install with vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 both at 5.0.5: the 2116 unit tests, lint, typecheck, parity and the 100% v8 coverage thresholds all pass, but the Stryker mutation score drops from 85.23% (vitest 4.1.11) to 0.88% on the same machine with --concurrency 4 (40 killed, 4482 survived). Cause: @stryker-mutator/vitest-runner 10.0.0, the latest release (14 Aug 2026, before vitest 5 on 3 Sep), builds its per-test testNamePattern from names joined with a single space (collectTestName, duplicated in test-helpers.js and stryker-setup.js), while vitest 5 matches the pattern against names joined with " > ". No test runs for a covered mutant, so it survives. Upstream issues: stryker-mutator/stryker-js 6210, 6262 and 6263 (fix proposed in 6214, not released). coverageAnalysis all or off and vitest.related false do not help. Changing the separator in both copies takes xml-parser.ts from 0% to 78%, against 85% on vitest 4, so even that patch does not reach parity. The mutation break threshold stays at 90 and is not lowered. Also, @vitest/coverage-v8 pins the exact vitest version as a peer: with vitest 5.0.3 and coverage-v8 4.1.11 the run fails with "Expected string coverage payload, received object" (53 errors), which is why the separate Dependabot PRs 134 and 136 could never pass. Implemented in PR #144: .github/dependabot.yml ignores semver-major for vitest and @vitest/*, and a dependabot group "vitest" (patterns vitest and @vitest/*, with exclude-patterns on the npm group) makes them arrive in one PR; the first grouped PR (#145, 4.1.11 to 4.1.12) was merged. PRs 134 and 136 were closed with a comment citing stryker-js 6210. To revisit when a vitest-runner release fixes the filter: remove the two ignore entries, bump vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 together, and measure the mutation score, not only npm test.
payload.title: Hold vitest below 5 until Stryker's vitest-runner is fixed; keep vitest and @vitest/* moving together
